labelled_by: Claude (on behalf of Ruhan), by reading the code at the pinned commit; needs an independent second-person spot check

queries.text: InvalidSchema: No connection adapters were found for 'ftp://example.com/file'

gold.why: sessions.py is the only place (besides a SOCKS-missing guard) that raises InvalidSchema with this exact message, after no mounted prefix matches the URL.

queries.text: CookieConflictError: There are multiple cookies with name 'sessionid'

gold.why: cookies.py raises CookieConflictError with exactly this message when more than one cookie matches name/domain/path.

queries.text: requests.exceptions.MissingSchema: Invalid URL 'example.com/api': No scheme supplied. Perhaps you meant https://example.com/api?

gold.why: models.py raises MissingSchema with this message when parse_url returns no scheme.

queries.text: A file upload that was partly read is not sent again from the beginning after the server answers with a redirect, so the second request goes out with a truncated body or the library gives up saying it cannot replay the body.

gold.why: utils.py seeks the body back to the recorded _body_position and raises UnrewindableBodyError when it cannot.
sessions.py: decides `rewindable` from _body_position and Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding and calls rewind_body before re-sending on each hop.

queries.text: Sending an empty POST without any payload makes some servers answer 411 length required because no length header is present on the outgoing message.

gold.why: models.py sets Content-Length to 0 for methods other than GET/HEAD when there is no body; this is the logic that governs the header.

queries.text: My script logs in to a website and gets bounced to a different website; afterwards my login details show up in that other website's access logs.

gold.why: sessions.py: compares old and new hostname/scheme/port to decide whether the Authorization header must be removed on a redirect.
sessions.py: deletes the Authorization header on redirect when should_strip_auth says so, then re-applies netrc credentials.

queries.text: The text of the web page comes out with garbled accented letters when the server does not say which character set it uses.

gold.why: models.py: decodes content using self.encoding, falling back to apparent_encoding, with errors='replace'; wrong guess yields mojibake.
utils.py returns ISO-8859-1 for text/* without a charset, which is the usual source of garbled UTF-8 pages.

queries.text: session.get() to the intranet address 10.0.0.5 goes through the corporate proxy although my no_proxy variable lists 10.0.0.0/8.

gold.why: utils.py evaluates no_proxy (host suffix, IP and CIDR forms) and decides whether to skip proxies; reached from Session.send via resolve_proxies.
utils.py is the CIDR membership test that should_bypass_proxies uses for IPv4 hosts when no_proxy contains a network.

queries.text: requests.post(url, json={'score': float('nan')}) fails with an error about out of range float values not being JSON compliant.

gold.why: models.py calls complexjson.dumps(json, allow_nan=False) and wraps ValueError into InvalidJSONError; reached via post -> request -> prepare_request -> prepare.

queries.text: session.get(url, headers={'X-Token': 'abc\n'}) raises InvalidHeader about return characters in the header value.

gold.why: utils.py raises InvalidHeader 'Invalid leading whitespace, reserved character(s), or return character(s) in header value' when the validator regex does not match.
utils.py is the entry that validates name and value; called from PreparedRequest.prepare_headers.

queries.text: I set session.verify = False but HTTPS calls still fail certificate verification as soon as REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is set in the environment.

gold.why: sessions.py: when verify is True/None it substitutes REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or CURL_CA_BUNDLE, then merges with the session setting; the environment value wins over the session default.
sessions.py decides which of request vs session setting is used; for non-dict values the request-level setting (here the env bundle) is returned.

queries.text: How is the maximum number of redirects configured? I raised the limit but the exception about too many redirects still appears at thirty.

gold.why: sessions.py sets self.max_redirects = DEFAULT_REDIRECT_LIMIT (30), the configurable default.
sessions.py: raises TooManyRedirects when len(resp.history) >= self.max_redirects.

queries.text: With many threads I get warnings that the connection pool is full and connections are discarded; where do I set pool size, blocking and retries for the transport?

gold.why: adapters.py takes pool_connections, pool_maxsize, max_retries, pool_block and stores them.
adapters.py builds the urllib3 PoolManager from num_pools/maxsize/block.

queries.text: Proxy credentials embedded in the proxy address (http://user:pass@proxy:3128) are not applied correctly: the Proxy-Authorization header is missing for plain HTTP targets after a redirect.

gold.why: adapters.py builds Proxy-Authorization from get_auth_from_url(proxy) for the proxy manager.
sessions.py: deletes and re-adds Proxy-Authorization on each redirect hop for non-https schemes.
utils.py extracts username/password from the proxy URL used by both of the above.

queries.text: Cookies that a server sets on a redirect response are not sent on the next hop of the redirect chain.

gold.why: sessions.py: pops Cookie, calls extract_cookies_to_jar and merge_cookies, then prepare_cookies for each hop.
cookies.py copies Set-Cookie headers from the urllib3 response into the jar; returns silently when _original_response is missing.
cookies.py merges the session jar into the request jar for the redirected request.
